name: Crackhead Control to Mission Control
description: Returning to Mission Control lowers the reinforcing leg from Crackhead Control while retaining the first high shin and hand connection to manage the opponent's posture.
summary: Returning to Mission Control lowers the reinforcing leg from Crackhead Control while retaining the first high shin and hand connection to manage the opponent's posture.
overview:
The bottom player has a two-leg high clinch with the opponent facing them. The change removes the second-leg reinforcement; it does not convert a rear ride or a leg entanglement into guard.

Maintain the original high leg and supporting hand before opening the second leg. Use the hip angle to support the raised knee without pulling on the foot. Lower the second leg deliberately while keeping the upper-body connection.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).

attacker.name: Crackhead Control to Mission Control Attacker
attacker.description: Crackhead Control to Mission Control (attacker): Maintain the original high leg and supporting hand before opening the second leg. Use the hip angle to support the raised knee without pulling on the foot.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player has a two-leg high clinch with the opponent facing them. The change removes the second-leg reinforcement; it does not convert a rear ride or a leg entanglement into guard.

Maintain the original high leg and supporting hand before opening the second leg. Use the hip angle to support the raised knee without pulling on the foot. Lower the second leg deliberately while keeping the upper-body connection.

Return the free foot or leg to a comfortable guard frame instead of leaving both hips uncontrolled. Recognize that the opponent may still have both arms inside and can rebuild posture. Recover ordinary guard if the first high-leg connection no longer holds safely.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Open the reinforcing leg while retaining the first high-leg posture control. If an overhook around the cleared arm is available, keep it connected to the knee during the change; the resulting Mission Control can support a later submission entry only after its own arm or neck controls are established.

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): Which connection stays while the second leg opens?
flashcards.answer: Maintain the first high-leg and hand connection as the second-leg reinforcement is removed.
flashcards.answer_line: First high shin held by its hand

plausible: First shin high with hand released
Only the second leg behind the head
trap: Only wrist grip with first knee open

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): How do you support the raised knee during the change?
flashcards.answer: Use hip angle to support the raised knee instead of pulling on the foot.
flashcards.answer_line: Hips angled with the knee close

plausible: Flat hip; pull the foot inward
Knee falls wide with shin still high
trap: Turn torso; hip and knee stay behind

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): Which leg moves down in the return?
flashcards.answer: Lower the reinforcing leg deliberately while keeping the original high shin connected.

plausible: The first high leg held by your hand
Both legs before checking the grip
trap: Second leg plus the first shin grip

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): Where should the newly freed leg become useful?
flashcards.answer: Return the free leg or foot to a comfortable lower guard frame while maintaining the upper connection.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower guard frame at the hip line

plausible: Extended beside you without contact
Still high behind the head
trap: Outside the hip with knee trailing

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): Arms start inside; what remains if only the second leg lowers?
flashcards.answer: Both arms may still be inside after the reinforcing leg lowers; track them because they can help recover posture.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside arms can frame for posture

plausible: Both elbows clear the first shin
The lowered leg still pins both arms
trap: An open knee hug isolates one arm

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): The first shin no longer controls posture; what next?
flashcards.answer: If the remaining high connection fails, rebuild ordinary guard instead of forcing the leg back into place.

plausible: Pull foot up without knee support
Low leg out; reach for their head
trap: Keep knee outside; chase their wrist

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): What body relationship remains throughout a successful return?
flashcards.answer: This is a reduction of high-leg reinforcement within facing guard, not a change to a rear ride or top headlock.

plausible: Bottom guard with shoulders away
Bottom guard with opponent far away
trap: Bottom guard with both legs low

flashcards.question: Return to Mission Control: which supported leg remains in the reviewed return?
flashcards.answer: Mission Control retains the original high shin and hand while the second leg returns lower.
flashcards.answer_line: First high shin; second leg lowered

plausible: Both legs high with hand grip open
Second leg high while first drops
trap: Both legs low before gripping shin

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): The raised knee is twisting as the second leg lowers; what now?
flashcards.answer: If the knee twists, release the high-leg tension and adjust through the hip or reset to ordinary guard.
flashcards.answer_line: Release tension; reset the hip angle

plausible: Knee fixed; draw the foot inward
High foot fixed; turn the torso
trap: Move low leg; keep high leg tense

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (bottom): An isolated-arm overhook exists; how can it stay connected?
flashcards.answer: If an overhook is already available, maintain its knee connection during the leg change; do not infer it from high legs alone.
flashcards.answer_line: Overhook close to the supported knee

plausible: Knee drifting away from the overhook
Release first shin to chase wrist
trap: Overhook elbow far from the knee

defender.description: Crackhead Control to Mission Control (defender): Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
defender.overview:
The bottom player has a two-leg high clinch with the opponent facing them. The change removes the second-leg reinforcement; it does not convert a rear ride or a leg entanglement into guard.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.

Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm. Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck. Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Use the opening between the two high-leg configurations as an early escape opportunity for the shoulder line. Keep the elbow inside before arm isolation develops, and tap if a submission connection is already loaded.

Recognize the reinforcement: A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
Control the hip line early: Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.
Clear the upper enclosure: Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm.
Keep a safe spine: Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck.
Pass after release: Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (top): As the second leg lowers, how should your elbow recover?
flashcards.answer: Use the changing leg configuration to recover an inside elbow while the shoulder is still free to move.
flashcards.answer_line: Inward toward ribs through the gap

plausible: Straight past the remaining knee
Elbow outside; retract only wrist
trap: Pull elbow against a fixed shoulder

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (top): Why can lowering one high leg leave posture restricted?
flashcards.answer: Removal of the second leg does not remove the original Mission Control connection.
flashcards.answer_line: First shin and hand hold you low

plausible: Low leg supplies all head control
Low ankle crossing holds shoulders
trap: Second foot alone holds the head

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (top): Which opening lets an early frame check the hip line as a leg lowers?
flashcards.answer: Use early inside space at the hip or thigh while preserving a balanced base.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside at the hip or thigh

plausible: Above the remaining high shin
Outside the elbow beside the mat
trap: Behind the hand holding the shin

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (top): What must release before you stand tall after the leg lowers?
flashcards.answer: Clear the retained high connection before lifting the head and chest through it.
flashcards.answer_line: Remaining high shin at the shoulder

plausible: Only the already-lowered second leg
Only their low foot off your hip
trap: Only their grip on your free wrist

flashcards.question: Crackhead to Mission (top): What can forward pressure do while the first leg still traps your arm?
flashcards.answer: Retained arm control must be addressed directly; stacking the partner is not evidence that the high connection has opened.
flashcards.answer_line: Neck folds; your arm stays caught

plausible: Forward weight frees the held elbow
Folding hips opens their shin grip
trap: Tight knee lets arm follow the chest
